title: Bias from polynomial field pairings
statement: Let $\ell>0$, let $a$ assign to each element $r$ of the binary extension field $\mathbb F_{2^\ell}$ a vector of $d$ elements of that field, and let $p$ assign to each $d$-coordinate binary vector a polynomial over $\mathbb F_{2^\ell}$. Suppose every polynomial $p(\gamma)$ with $\gamma\ne0$ is nonzero, its value at every $r$ equals $\sum_i\gamma_i a(r)_i$, and its degree is at most $D$. The probability density obtained by choosing two field elements independently and uniformly and generating the binary vector from their pairings with $a$ is biased: every nonzero Fourier coefficient has absolute value at most $D/2^\ell$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ maps each field element to a $d$-tuple over the binary extension field
$p$ assigns a polynomial to every $d$-coordinate binary vector
